rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong reference point by testing the most complete multimodal configuration. config_039 combines all the most expressive components: multimodal fusion (leveraging both RNA and image), multiprofile (richer cellular representation), scgpt (learned context-aware RNA encoder), imagenet_vit_l (strong pretrained vision encoder), transformer aggregation (most flexible multi-profile combination), and weighted fusion (learned modality balancing). This tests whether the full pipeline yields high validation accuracy, giving me a strong baseline to compare against. In subsequent experiments, I can systematically ablate individual components (e.g., swap scgpt→pca, imagenet_vit_l→resnet50, transformer→avgpool, or drop to single-modality) to identify which design choices drive performance. Starting here maximizes information gain per experiment under the 10-run budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_039: multimodal, scgpt+imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → acc 0.52), the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion is actually contributing meaningful signal over a single-modality baseline. Config_001 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) is the natural RNA-only counterpart that keeps the same RNA encoder and aggregation strategy, isolating the effect of the image modality. If RNA alone performs comparably (~0.50-0.52), the search can focus on refining the RNA pipeline or testing simpler image encoders; if it performs substantially worse, it confirms the value of multimodal fusion and justifies further exploration of fusion strategies and image encoders. This is the highest-information experiment at this stage because it partitions the 8 remaining experiments between two very different search strategies (optimize multimodal fusion vs. optimize single-modality model), and the answer is unlikely to be resolved by tweaking secondary knobs like fusion type or aggregation.

Evidence: The best multimodal config (config_039: scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves only 0.520 accuracy vs 0.514 for RNA-only, and notably has a worse F1 (0.479 vs 0.498), suggesting the weighted fusion may be diluting useful RNA signal with image noise. Question: config_009 is a single-variable ablation of config_039, changing only fusion from weighted to concat while keeping scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, and multiprofile fixed. This directly tests whether the fusion mechanism is the bottleneck preventing the image modality from contributing meaningfully. Why this is the best next experiment: With only 2 data points and a very small accuracy gap, the highest-priority uncertainty is whether the current multimodal pipeline can be made to clearly outperform the RNA-only baseline. Isolating the fusion choice (the most tunable hyperparameter in the fusion step) is the most information-dense single experiment. If concat improves accuracy and F1, it validates the multimodal direction and guides remaining budget toward concat-based variants; if it doesn't, it shifts focus to image encoder or RNA encoder choices.

Evidence: config_039 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) is the best at 0.5200 acc, but we have only tested one RNA encoder (scgpt). The RNA encoder is a fundamental representation choice that could significantly impact downstream fusion quality. Question: Does scvi_n200 (a learned VAE-based representation) perform comparably to or better than scgpt when paired with the same imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted pipeline? Why this is the best next experiment: It is a clean single-variable ablation of the best configuration, directly reducing uncertainty about whether the scgpt encoder is specifically critical or whether any strong learned RNA representation works. With 6 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out the RNA encoder choice early will focus subsequent experiments on the remaining high-impact dimensions (image encoder, aggregation) rather than wasting budget on a suboptimal RNA representation.

The dominant finding is that swapping the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 (config_039→config_014) produced a massive ~20-point accuracy jump (0.520→0.725) while keeping imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion constant. This strongly implicates scvi_n200 as the key driver. The next logical exploitation step is to test whether the image encoder also matters: config_032 keeps the proven scvi_n200 + transformer + weighted stack but swaps imagenet_vit_l for resnet50. This single-variable change will clarify whether the 0.725 is robust to image encoder choice or whether imagenet_vit_l is specifically synergistic with scvi_n200. If resnet50 performs comparably, we gain flexibility for future experiments; if it degrades significantly, we confirm imagenet_vit_l is critical and should focus remaining budget on aggregation/fusion variants around the config_014 core. With 5 experiments left, this targeted test maximizes information gain while staying in the high-performing region.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_014, acc=0.725) is the best configuration by a wide margin over all scgpt-based runs (~0.52). The only untested variable within this top-performing regime is the fusion method: we have only tested 'weighted' with scvi_n200+ViT-L. Config_036 changes only the fusion from weighted to concat, directly testing whether the fusion mechanism matters when the RNA encoder is strong. With scgpt, weighted (0.520) barely beat concat (0.507), but that regime was overall weak; the dynamics may differ with scvi_n200. Resolving this single-variable question is critical before spending remaining budget on other axes (aggregation, image encoder), because it determines the architectural template for any further exploitation. With 4 experiments left, locking down the best fusion for the top encoder pair is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step.

The top performer is config_014 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy, with config_036 (same but concat fusion) at 0.7207 and config_032 (resnet50, weighted) at 0.7131. The RNA encoder (scvi_n200) and image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) choices are well-supported. The remaining key uncertainty in the top-performing region is whether the transformer aggregation is truly necessary or whether a simpler avgpool aggregation could perform comparably. Config_033 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is a direct single-variable ablation of the best config, testing only the aggregation choice. This is the highest-information experiment: if avgpool matches transformer, it confirms architectural robustness and frees remaining budget for other refinements; if it drops significantly, it confirms transformer is critical and we should lock in that choice. With 3 experiments left after this, resolving this uncertainty is essential before committing to final exploitation runs.

The top-performing config (config_014: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted; acc=0.7250) has been thoroughly explored along image encoder, aggregation, and fusion dimensions, with all variants tested. The only major untested variable within this best architecture is the RNA encoder: pca_n2000 has never been evaluated in multimodal settings. Testing config_002 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) isolates the RNA encoder as the sole change from the best config. If PCA performs comparably, it reveals the RNA representation is not the bottleneck and we can confidently lock in scvi_n200 for the final experiment. If PCA is substantially worse, it confirms scvi_n200 is critical and directs the last experiment toward fine-tuning other dimensions (e.g., a hybrid or regularization variant). With only 2 experiments remaining, this single-variable test maximally reduces uncertainty about the most impactful architectural choice before committing the final budget slot.

The best result so far is config_014 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. All multiprofile+transformer variants with scvi_n200 have been tested and cluster around 0.71-0.725, suggesting we're near the ceiling for that architecture. The key untested direction is the singleprofile setting (aggregation=None), which fundamentally changes how profiles are handled. Config_011 pairs the two best-performing encoders (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l) with the best fusion method (weighted) under the singleprofile architecture. This tests whether reducing architectural complexity (no transformer aggregation over multiple profiles) could yield a cleaner signal and potentially exceed 0.725, or at minimum clarify whether the multiprofile+transformer advantage is real or an artifact. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the most structurally distinct yet component-optimal configuration maximizes both the chance of a breakthrough and the information gained.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + transformer aggregation is the dominant high-performing combination (0.725, 0.721, 0.713 across tested image/fusion pairings). The best config (config_014: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.725, while resnet50+transformer+weighted (config_032) reaches 0.713 with notably higher F1 (0.695 vs 0.685), suggesting resnet50 features may interact differently with fusion strategies. Question: Does concat fusion with resnet50+transformer+scvi_n200 close or exceed the 0.725 gap? With imagenet_vit_l, concat was only 0.4% below weighted (0.721 vs 0.725), but resnet50's higher F1 under weighted fusion hints its feature space may pair more favorably with concat. Why this is the best last experiment: It is the only untested combination of the two top-performing components (scvi_n200, transformer) with a different image encoder/fusion pairing, offering the highest probability of discovering a configuration that matches or exceeds the current best of 0.725 while also reducing uncertainty about the resnet50+concat interaction.
